#### **<u>Highlights</u>** 

##### **China’s power supply and demand in a basic balance, but a large growth fall** 

China's electricity use, a key indicator of industrial activity, is expected to grow 6 to 7 percent in 2012 to fall between 4.98 trillion and 5.03 trillion kilowatt-hours, which is largely lower than preliminary forecast mainly due to large fall of economic growth in the first half of 2012 and greater downward pressure than previous expectations. With regards to power supply, it is expected that newly added power energy capacity will be 86 GW in 2012, including 20 GW of hydropower and 50 GW thermal power. 

In the first half of 2012, newly added power energy capacity was 25.85 GW, down 8.92 GW compared with the same period of 2011. In the first half of 2012, newly added power energy capacity of thermal power decreased 7.44 G

W compared with the same period of 2011. 

China's power consumption growth slumped significantly in the first half of the year amid an economic slowdown, according to data released by the China Electricity Council (CEC). In the first six months, total power consumption grew just 5.5 percent from a year earlier, dragged down by a sharp decline in power use by industrial and high energy-consuming industries, the CEC said in a report. 

But the third-tier industry and residential power consumption expanded fast during the period, the CEC noted. However, a greater chance of economic growth picking up over the second half means power demand is likely to rebound in subsequent months. The CEC projected total power consumption to grow between 6 and 8 percent year-on-year to hit between 2.6 trillion and 2.65 trillion kilowatt-hours in the second half. The CEC said the country will see a general surplus in power supply during the summer peak season for electricity, and power shortages will be less stressful in energy-strapped regions. 

In the first year of 2012, China’s trans-provincial and trans-regional power output increased by 8.0% and 18.7% YoY, respectively. 18 Chinese regions conducted trades of power generation rights in the first half, with a transaction volume of 35.7 billion kWh, almost the same as that of last year. The transaction of power generation rights has helped cut the use of 2.63 million metric tons of standard coal equivalent, or 6.84 million tons of carbon emissions, the report said. Generally, wind and coal electricity in Northeast China and the Inner Mongolia autonomous region is sold to North China, while hydropower in Central China is delivered to South and East China. Coal-generated electricity in the northwest is supplied to Central and North China.

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

##### **Copper prices fluctuate in a relative broad range in July** 

In July, copper prices fluctuated in a relative broad range. Economic trend in China, US and European zone was still the main factor which influenced copper price and would continue to make influence on copper market confidence and lead the trend of global copper prices. 

In July, LME copper cash average price and 3-M average price were USD7,589/t and USD7,590/t, up 2.28% and 2.29% m/m, but down by 21.10% and 21.26% y/y. 

LME copper stocks lingered over 250kt during much of July, but fell below this point at the end of July. Copper stocks growth in Korea Pusan warehouse obviously slowed down, almost stagnated near the middle of July and began to fall continuously in late July. But cancelled warrants increased to about 50kt from 27kt in early July, accounting for about 20% of the total copper stocks. 

In July, SHFE copper prices ever climbed to over 56,000 yuan/t, but were blocked at 56,500 yuan/t. After that, under the pressure of LME copper prices falling, SHFE copper price fell below 55,000 yua

n/t and then obtained support at the point of 54,000 yuan/t. In July, SHFE copper cash average price and 3-M average price were 55,485 yuan/t and 5,5420 yuan/t, up 1.138% and 1.39% m/m, but down by 22.62% and 22.77% y/y. 

Near the end of July, SHFE copper stocks increased to about 160kt, most of which were from the bonded warehouse. Copper prices had no much change facing the rising copper stocks on SHFE, due to high level of copper stock taken for granted for Chinese copper investors. 

On spot market, copper consumption was weak and market transactions were small. With regards to copper scrap market, copper scrap supply was still tight and most of downstream buyers were lack of buy confidence. 

On August 1, China's final HSBC manufacturing PMI climbed to 49.3 in July from 48.2 reading in June, its highest level since February but still below 50, the threshold dividing expansion from Contraction. 

From a technical point of view, several average lines formed a certain pressure and copper price was lack of enough rebounding power, dragged by the worrying macro trend. On the whole, copper market was lack of clear direction and copper would fluctuate at a relative wide range in the next two month.

##### **Chinese refined copper production steadily rises** 

According to data from China Nonferrous metals Industry Association (CNIA), in June, domestic refined copper output reached 493kt, up by 7.2% MoM and by 7.4% YoY. Refined copper output amounted to 2.77Mt during Jan to Jun, up by 10.6% YoY. According to data from National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), refined copper output in June reached 518kt, up by 7.0% MoM and 11.6% YoY; refined copper output during Jan to Jun amounted to 2.92Mt, up by 10.3% YoY. Besides, according to Antaike’s survey, copper cathode output in domestic 12 refiners reached 337.4kt in June, up by 3.49% MoM; copper cathode output in domestic 12 refiners was 1.98Mt, up by 4.72% YoY. We generally thought refined copper output released by the NBS and CNIA were larger than the actual. But the overall data showed the similar growth trend. 

Data from the CNIA still showed that domestic copper semis output was 1.08Mt in June, with a month on month rise of 10.5% and year on year rise of 9.9%; copper semis output amounted to 5.41Mt during Jan to Jun, up by 10.1% YoY. Seen from growth trend of copper semis output, domestic copper consumption was not too gloomy. 



##### **Chinese refined copper imports have m-o-m fall in June, but exports stay high** 

Statistics released by China’s Customs showed that refined copper import was 250kt in Jun, down by 17.2% MoM but up by 40.2% YoY; during Jan to Jun, refined copper import amounted to 1.88Mt, up by 73.6% YoY. High level of refined copper import was also one of the main reasons led to current supply surplus, besides weak demand in domestic copper market. Afte

r continuous interest rate cut and reduction in deposit reserve rate, as well as narrowing arbitrage between RMB and USD, refined copper import will be influenced at a certain degree in the near future. It is estimated that refined copper import won’t be

Refined copper export had a month on month down of 65.4% in Jun. Refined copper export reached 35kt in Jun, up by 1057.3% YoY, with net import no much change compared with that in May. 

Copper scraps import was 369kt in Jun, down by 12.9% MoM. Copper scrap import amounted to 2.23Mt during Jan to Jun, up by 1.3% YoY. Current domestic copper scraps market was in supply shortage and at the same time, downstream consumption was weak. Most of downstream manufacturers and traders purchase with caution, especially under the situation of no upside sign for current copper price. 

Copper concentrate import was 481kt in Jun, down by 28.0% MoM and 19.0% YoY. Copper concentrate import amounted to 3.38Mt during Jan to Jun, at a year on year rise of 14.9%. Due to China’s high dependence on foreign raw materials, as well as domestic copper scraps supply in shortage, copper concentrate import will likely rebound in July.

##### **Copper consumption** 

According to data from the NBS, most copper end-using copper products output decreased during Jan to Jun, except output of power cable, transformer, air conditioner and autos had year on year rise. Above data showed that such traditional copper consuming sectors, as electric power industry and air conditioning industry still barely supported Chinese copper consumption. It is not to be neglected that growth rate of air conditioner output has been obviously slowed down. During Jan to Jun of 2012, growth rate of air conditioner output increased by 1.5% YoY, while at 41.8% in the same period of 2011. So, air conditioning industry won’t give much support for copper consumption in the future. 

According to data from China Electricity Council, in H1 2012, the completed power investment increased by 2.3% YoY, while at 9.1% in H1 2011. Among them, investment in power grid rose by 8.0% YoY, but investment in power generation down by 2.6% YoY. Of power generation investment, investment in wind power and thermal power declined by 37.3% and 16.8% YoY, respectively.

Investment proportion of thermal power investment in power generation power was 4.7 percentage points lower than the same period of 2011. Investment in nuclear power decreased by 5.1% YoY, due to no newly-commenced projects happened since 2011. 

But Antaike believed that electric power industry would still be a stronger power for copper consumption in H2 2012. In H1 2012, completed investment in rural power network reached 1.69 billion yuan, accounting for only 3.73% of the planned investment in whole 2012. Besides,

grid bidding will be launched again in Q3. During Jan to Jun, investment in domestic real estate development was 3.06 trillion yuan, nominal up by 16.6% YoY (real growth of 14.3%), 1.9 percentage points lower than that in Jan to May. Among them, investment in residential houses was 2.09 trillion yuan, up by 12.0% YoY, 1.6 percentage points lower than that in Jan to May, accounting for 68.2% of the total investment in real estate. During Jan to Jun, floor space under construction was 4,756.14 mln sq.m, up by 17.2% YoY, 2.4 percentage points lower than that in Jan to May. Of them, floor space under construction of residential houses was 3,573.92 mln sq.m, at a rise of 15.0% YoY. Starting floor space of houses was 923.80 mln sq.m, down by 7.1% YoY, of which starting floor space of residential houses was 686.17 mln sq.m, down by 10.7% YoY. Completion floor space of houses was 332.59 mln sq.m, up by 20.7% YoY, 5.6 percentage points lower than that in Jan to May, of which completion floor space of residential houses was 267.19 mln sq.m, up by 21.1% YoY. On the whole, obvious growth slowdown in real estate industry gave a certain pressure on copper consumption. Data trend of Chinese real estate industry have some influence on copper prices although it is not important copper consuming sector in China. According to the statement from State Council, housing purchase restriction policy will remain unchanged, which increased pessimism on copper market. Several refiners was doing overhauling works during this period, which made influence on domestic refined copper output in the first half of the year. Output of domestic 12 refiners accounted for over 70% of domestic production. Besides, overhauling works will be launched one after another in some of China’s northern copper refiners. In the next two month, domestic copper consumption will improve at a certain degree, but won’t be strong. Domestic supply surplus basically depends on how much will be imported.
